about: the 'against git itself' cases cannot be passed or failed by the host's git config: every line of the isolation is needed against a hostile host played on every machine, and each route that host uses really does rewrite the push URL

mutants.find: * The host that broke this file, played on every machine.
mutants.replace: * The host that broke this file, played on any machine.
mutants.why: a no-op: a doc comment reworded, nothing a test can see
the isolation as a whole: without it the host's rewrite reaches git and the separate push URL collapses into the fetch URL
GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS is deleted: a parent git -c hands its flags down through it
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, KEY_n and VALUE_n are deleted: the route the 2026-10-11 container used
GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM skips the system file, whatever GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM names
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null replaces the user's global file
the premise: a route that no longer rewrites anything is caught, not left as a guard that proves nothing
